A. Daily inspection before use
1. Confirm the operator carries a current manufacturer qualification card for this tool model.
2. Tool is unloaded before any inspection. Check the chamber and strip guide are empty.
3. Check the piston and buffer for chips, mushrooming or cracks. Replace if damaged.
4. Check the fastener guide and muzzle for wear and that the guide is fully seated.
5. Press the muzzle against a hard surface: the tool must not cycle unless fully depressed. Test the contact-pressure safety three times.
6. Check the power regulator wheel turns and clicks at each setting.
7. Wipe carbon from the piston return and strip guide. Follow the cleaning interval on the tool case label.
8. Confirm fasteners and booster strips on hand are the type listed for this tool. Do not mix brands.
9. Post the warning sign at the work area entrance.

B. Choosing booster strength
- Always start with the lowest strength on hand and the regulator at its lowest setting, and make one test fastening.
- If the pin stands proud, raise the regulator one step at a time. Only move to the next strength when the regulator is already at maximum.
- Strength order from low to high is green, yellow, red. Typical starting point is yellow for normal-weight concrete and red for structural steel, confirmed by the test fastening.
- Do not fasten into concrete thinner than three times the pin penetration, within 3 in. of an edge, or into steel thinner than the pin shank diameter or within 1/2 in. of an edge.
- Never fasten into cast iron, glazed tile, hardened steel, glass block or hollow tile.

C. Tool does not drive after the trigger is pulled
1. Keep the tool pressed firmly against the work surface for at least 30 seconds.
2. Keep the muzzle pointed at the work surface and away from people while lifting it off.
3. Advance the strip one position by cycling the tool per the manual and try again.
4. If it fails a second time, hold 30 seconds again, remove the strip, and place the strip in a bucket of water.
5. Tag the tool out and report it to the superintendent. Do not pry out a booster with any object.

Reference: 29 CFR 1926.302(e). "FILE NOTE ER-2026-0417. Prepared by: Lerato Mokoena, HR Generalist, Medivest Pharmaceutical Distributors (Pty) Ltd, Midrand. Date and time of note: Thursday 17 September 2026, 14:30. Purpose: to record the facts as they are known at this time regarding a post on the staff Wellness Corner forum. This note records what was posted, by whom, what has been said since, and the documents that bear on it. It does not make a finding.

1. The forum. Wellness Corner is a forum on the company intranet, open to all 1,940 staff, launched in March 2023. Members post under handles. The banner shown to every new member since launch reads: 'This is your space. Share what worked for you. You are not alone.' The forum guidelines, last revised in January 2025, include the following. Section 4: 'Speak from your own experience. Do not tell another member what medicine to take or how much.' Section 7: 'A moderator may redact part of a post and leave a visible note, or may remove a post entirely. The author is told either way.' Section 9: 'Handles are not linked to staff numbers. The forum administrator will look up who is behind a handle only where a member may be at risk of harm.' The forum is moderated by the Wellness Coordinator, Ms Anneke Botha. A digest of the week's most-read threads is e-mailed to all staff every Friday at 07:00. The thread in question is currently the most-read thread of the week.

2. The thread. On Monday 14 September a member using the handle Bra_S started a thread titled 'Nerve pain after shingles - anyone?'. He wrote that he had been prescribed a medicine for the pain and was not sleeping.

3. The post. On Wednesday 16 September at 21:12 a member using the handle ThandiM_DC2 replied. The post is reproduced in full: 'I don't usually post. I had the same thing after shingles in 2024. My doctor put me on pregabalin 75 mg twice a day. First two weeks, nothing. She moved me to 150 twice a day and that is when it turned. The 150 knocked me flat for the first week, I was walking into door frames, then it settled. Honestly, if the 75 is doing nothing for you, just take two of them at night, that is where your doctor will end up anyway and you will finally sleep. Whatever you do, don't stop it cold. I did that once and it was the worst three days of my life. Speak to your doctor before you come off it. Also ask at the pharmacy about the generic, it is on our medical aid formulary and the co-payment is much less. I nearly didn't post this. It is the first time I have said anything about my health at work. Hang in there, it does get better.'

4. Responses on the thread. On Thursday 17 September at 11:48 Bra_S replied: 'Thanks sis. Three weeks on the 75s and nothing. Will try two tonight. I'm on nights this week so tonight means before I clock in at 22:00, the reach truck doesn't drive itself lol.' Three other members have marked the post 'saving this'. One further member wrote: 'My mom is on the same one, I will tell her.' Bra_S is subscribed to the thread. Thread notifications go to members' work e-mail. Warehouse staff without desks read work e-mail at the shared kiosk in the canteen.

5. The author. The handle ThandiM_DC2 contains the author's first name and site and she has confirmed authorship. She is Ms Thandeka Mahlangu, Picker, Schedule 5 and 6 cage, Distribution Centre 2. Six years' service. No disciplinary record. Ms Botha sent her a direct message at 12:20 today. Ms Mahlangu replied at 12:51: 'Please fix it however you need to. I didn't think. Should I delete it?' She has not been given an answer yet. On 4 February 2019 Ms Mahlangu signed the acknowledgement of the Medicines Information Policy, which states: 'Employees who are not registered pharmacists must not give advice on the dose or use of any medicine to any person in the course of their employment or on company platforms.' HR records show no briefing to staff on how that policy relates to the forum, at the forum's launch or since.

6. Information from the Responsible Pharmacist. Mr Pieter van Wyk provided the following by e-mail at 13:10: pregabalin is a Schedule 5 medicine; a change from 150 mg to 300 mg per day is a decision for the prescriber; drowsiness and dizziness are listed in the package insert as very common; the package insert advises against abrupt discontinuation. He also noted that the company's wholesale licence inspection by SAHPRA is scheduled for November 2026.

7. Previous matter. In May 2024 a sales representative received a written warning after posting dosing guidance for an antibiotic in a public Facebook group for clinic managers. His profile named the company, and the group's members were customers.

8. Forum statistics, for reference. In June 2025 a post in a thread on antidepressants was removed in full by the moderator. Posts in health-related threads in the two months that followed numbered 61, against 127 in the two months before. One post has been redacted with a note since launch, in October 2025; posts in the two months either side numbered 118 and 112.

9. Operations. The DC2 night shift roster for this week lists three reach-truck drivers. The shift starts at 22:00. The Night Shift Supervisor is Mr Bongani Dube, on site from 21:30.

Recorded by L. Mokoena. Circulated to: Ms A. Botha; Mr P. van Wyk; Ms N. Pillay, Head of Employee Relations."

1. Batch details
Course: Disruption Handling and Rebooking, Level 2 (DHR-2), for airport passenger services agents. Delivered at the Sahab Airways Training Centre, Dubai Airport Freezone, on 24 and 25 August 2026 by the external provider, Meridian Aviation Training FZ-LLC. Two sessions ran in parallel. Session A was led by Mr. Tariq Al Hammadi with 71 attendees. Session B was led by Ms. Corinne D'Souza with 69 attendees. All 140 attendees returned an evaluation. Responses are anonymous and carry a respondent number only; there is no route back to an individual.

2. Form
Q1 to Q6 are ratings from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent): content, trainer, pace, materials, facilities, relevance to role. Q7: 'In one word, how was the course overall?' Q8: 'What could be improved?' Q9: 'What was most useful?' Q10: 'Anything else?' Q11: 'Would you recommend this course to a colleague?' (Yes / Maybe / No). Q7 to Q10 are free text and none of them is mandatory. On the form, Q7 and Q8 appear one directly under the other on the same screen.

3. Collection
Session A attendees received the form by emailed link and completed it on their own devices within 48 hours. For Session B the link emails bounced for 52 of the 69 attendees, who are agency staff without corporate mailboxes. Ms. D'Souza passed a training-centre tablet around the room during the last ten minutes of day two and all 69 completed it there. Average across Q1 to Q6: Session A 3.9, Session B 4.6. Respondent R-093 (Session B) wrote under Q10: 'Trainer was standing next to me while I filled this, so.'

4. Codebook v3 extract (Q8 codes)
NI - No improvement suggested: the respondent indicates that nothing should change. Examples: nothing, none, nil, all good as it is.
CT - Content. PC - Pace and timing. MT - Materials. FC - Facilities. TR - Trainer. OT - Other suggestion.
Note in codebook: bare adjectives describing the course are not listed under any code; coder to decide. A response may be recorded against a different question from the one it was typed under where the coder is satisfied that is where it belongs; the original field is then treated as unanswered.

5. Query 1 - respondent R-117 (Session A)
Q1 content 3. Q2 trainer 4. Q3 pace 2. Q4 materials 3. Q5 facilities 4. Q6 relevance 3.
Q7: (blank)
Q8: 'fine.'
Q9: 'The rebooking simulator. Rest was slides I had seen in induction.'
Q10: (blank)
Q11: Maybe
For reference, Q7 was answered by 138 of the 140 respondents; typical entries are 'useful', 'good', 'long', 'fine', 'intense'. Both of R-117's text entries end with a full stop. In the July batch I coded 'fine' under Q8 as NI on four occasions and these were passed at quality check. I propose to do the same for R-117.

6. Query 2 - short answers under Q8
23 of the 140 answers under Q8 are two words or fewer. Breakdown: 'nothing' 6, 'none' 4, 'nil' 3, 'no changes' 1 (total 14); 'good' 3, 'fine' 2 including R-117, 'ok' 2 (total 7); '-' 1 and '.' 1 (total 2). To save approximately 40 minutes I propose to run a macro that codes all 23 as NI in one pass. For information, the NI share is one of three figures on the provider scorecard that goes to the Head of Training for the Meridian renewal decision on 30 September. The scorecard also shows the Session A and Session B rating averages side by side, by trainer name.

7. Query 3 - collection method
I have not mentioned the difference in collection method anywhere in the handoff so far, as it is not a coding matter. The batch notes field is free text and is printed as a footnote on the scorecard. Kindly advise whether anything is to be added.

Awaiting your kind guidance.

A misconnect happens when a passenger's inbound flight arrives too late for him to make his onward flight. This guide walks through eligibility, options, rebooking, care, baggage and communication so that nothing is overlooked.

## Step 1: Confirm eligibility
Open the PNR and check three things. First, that KHI-LHE and LHE-DXB are on the same ticket number; they are, as you have said. Second, that the inbound delay is coded to the carrier; a 5 h 10 min late arrival on our own flight is. Third, that the passenger has presented himself at the transfer desk, which he has. With all three satisfied he counts as an involuntary misconnect under point 1 of the extract, and nothing that follows will cost him anything.

## Step 2: Understand the options
The extract gives two routes. The default is the next available flight of our own. Endorsement to a partner carrier is permitted only when no own flight departs within six hours. It is now 14:55 and IK 614 leaves at 17:30, which is inside six hours, so endorsement does not apply today and no duty manager signature is needed for it.

## Step 3: Rebook
In the DCS, open the PNR, choose Reaccommodate, select Involuntary, then pick IK 614 from the availability list. Set the reason code to MISC. Confirm the segment and reissue; the fare difference should show as zero. Check him in on the new segment and print the boarding pass. IK 614 is showing 9 seats and check-in closes at 16:30.

## Step 4: Care entitlements
Under point 3 a meal voucher is due when the wait between arrival and the new departure is more than two hours. He landed at 14:20 and will leave at 17:30, so one voucher of PKR 1,500 is due. Issue it from the Vouchers tab using type MEAL and hand him the printed slip; outlets on both sides of security accept it. Under point 4 a hotel is due only when the new departure falls on the next calendar day. His does not, so no hotel applies.

## Step 5: Baggage
His bag was tagged to DXB on the flight he missed. Send a retag request to the baggage room with the new flight number so that it is loaded on IK 614, and give him the new tag receipt.

## Step 6: Talking to the passenger
Apologise for the delay, tell him plainly what you have done and what time to be at the gate, and point him towards the food outlets. Passengers usually respond well to a clear timeline.

## If things change
If IK 614 fills before you confirm his seat, the picture changes: partner endorsement and possibly a hotel become relevant, and the duty manager should be called.

state: {"document": "Incident working note INC-PRV-2025-031, version 4", "organisation": "Wattle Rides Australia Pty Ltd", "prepared_by": "Imogen Farquharson, People & Culture generalist, seconded as incident scribe", "prepared_on": "Thursday 17 July 2025, 11:40 AEST", "for_meeting": "Incident review group, Thursday 17 July 2025, 14:00 AEST, Level 6 boardroom and video", "regulator_reference": "", "purpose_and_status": "This note brings together what has been recorded so far about the partner statement mis-delivery of Tuesday 15 July 2025, so that the incident review group can settle who is to be treated as affected in the first round of notification and remediation. It records what people have said and what the records show. It does not recommend a course of action. Where a person's view is recorded, it is attributed to that person and is theirs alone. The figure most often quoted in discussion to date is 1,100, being the number of driver-partners who received, by email, an annual earnings statement belonging to another driver-partner. That figure has been used in the chief executive's briefing of Wednesday, in the vendor's letter and in the contact centre script. All 1,100 had service addresses in the Brisbane metropolitan postcode band 4000 to 4179 and all were in a single vendor job. The meeting invitation lists the start time as 2.30pm; the room booking is for 14:00. Attendees may wish to confirm with Ms Okonkwo's office.", "background": "Each July the company issues every driver-partner (the customers of the statements service) an annual earnings statement for the financial year just ended. The statement is a two-page PDF. It shows the partner's full name, residential address, ABN, gross fares, service fees, tolls reimbursed, net earnings, and the BSB and last three digits of the bank account into which payouts were made. Since 2022 production and delivery has been outsourced to Corbel Print & Mail Pty Ltd of Eagle Farm under master services agreement MSA-2022-114. The company supplies Corbel with one merge file per job. Corbel generates the PDFs, attaches each to a delivery record, and delivers by one of two streams: e-delivery (email with the PDF attached) for partners who have a verified email address and have not opted out, and postal (printed, machine-enveloped and lodged with Australia Post) for the remainder. The two streams are fed from the same merge file and the same generated PDF set; a partner's row is routed to one stream or the other by a flag in the row. Rows are sorted by partner ID, so postal rows are scattered through the file rather than grouped. For the 2024-25 year the partner base was split into jobs by postcode band and onboarding date. Job CPM-250714-A covered partners with service addresses in postcodes 4000 to 4179 who were onboarded before 1 June 2025. It contained 5,042 rows: 4,830 flagged for e-delivery and 212 flagged for postal. Partners in the same postcode band onboarded on or after 1 June 2025 (318 partners) were placed in job CPM-250714-C together with late onboardings from other bands. Job CPM-250714-B covered postcodes 4200 to 4299 (Gold Coast and Logan), 3,916 rows. All three jobs were run on the night of Monday 14 July.", "sequence_of_events": ["Mon 14 July, 17:20. Partner Payments uploaded the three merge files to Corbel's secure transfer site. Upload receipts held on file.", "Mon 14 July, 22:05 to Tue 15 July, 01:48. Corbel generated PDFs for jobs A, B and C in that order.", "Tue 15 July, 02:10 to 03:35. E-delivery for job A was sent. Jobs B and C followed and completed by 05:20.", "Tue 15 July, 07:52. First contact received. A partner in Coorparoo telephoned the contact centre to say the statement attached to her email carried another person's name and a Woolloongabba address.", "Tue 15 July, 09:30. Eleven similar contacts had been logged. The contact centre team leader, Mr Bhattarai, raised a priority ticket with Partner Payments and with the Privacy Officer, Ms Delacroix.", "Tue 15 July, 10:15. Partner Payments telephoned Corbel's account manager, Mr Hallam, who undertook to investigate.", "Tue 15 July, 16:30. Corbel lodged the postal pieces for jobs A, B and C with Australia Post at the Northgate business hub, as scheduled. Lodgement receipt for job A shows 212 articles, regular letter service.", "Tue 15 July, 17:45. Mr Hallam telephoned to say the cause had been found in job A and that a written account would follow. No one present on the call recalls the postal lodgement being mentioned by either side.", "Wed 16 July, 09:00. Corbel's letter received (extract below).", "Wed 16 July, 11:30. The Data & Insights team began its own comparison (see internal verification).", "Wed 16 July, 15:00. Chief executive briefed by Ms Delacroix. The briefing paper states that 1,100 partners received another partner's statement and that the matter is confined to one job.", "Wed 16 July, 16:10. Data & Insights reported the result of its comparison for job A.", "Thu 17 July, 09:15. Data & Insights reported results for jobs B and C.", "Thu 17 July, 10:30. Australia Post's business line advised, in answer to a general enquiry from Mr Bhattarai about delivery times, that regular letters lodged at Northgate on a Tuesday afternoon for Brisbane metropolitan addresses are ordinarily delivered between the following Friday and the Tuesday after that."], "vendor_letter_extract": "From Corbel Print & Mail Pty Ltd, signed G. Hallam, Account Director, dated 16 July 2025. 'We write further to yesterday's conversations. Our production team has identified that row 3,897 of the merge file for job CPM-250714-A contained a line break within the partner name field. Our attachment step read that row as two records. From that row to the end of the file, each delivery record was paired with the document generated for the row that follows it. Rows 1 to 3,896 were unaffected by the misreading. We have reconciled the e-delivery stream in full by comparing the attachment hash recorded in the e-delivery log against the hash of the document generated for each recipient. Of 4,830 e-delivery records, 3,730 carry the correct document and 1,100 carry the document of another partner. We can therefore confirm that 1,100 partners received a statement that was not their own. The e-delivery stream is fully reconciled and we consider the extent of the matter to be established. We confirm that 212 postal articles for this job were lodged on 15 July in accordance with the production schedule. Jobs CPM-250714-B and CPM-250714-C were produced from separate merge files and our checks of those jobs have found no discrepancy. We have added a validation step that rejects any merge file containing control characters in a name field. We regret the inconvenience caused and remain available to assist.' The letter does not say anything further about the postal articles.", "internal_verification": "Ms Yeo of Data & Insights carried out the company's own comparison independently of Corbel. For job A she obtained Corbel's e-delivery log, which records for each email sent the row number, the recipient address and a SHA-256 hash of the attachment. She regenerated the expected hash for each of the 4,830 e-delivery rows from the company's own copy of the statement data and compared the two. Her result matches Corbel's: 3,730 rows where the hash is as expected, all of them at row numbers below 3,897, and 1,100 rows where it is not, all of them at row 3,897 or above. For each of the 1,100 she identified whose document was in fact attached. Of the 1,100 documents sent to the wrong person, 1,055 belong to partners who are themselves among the 1,100 email recipients, and 45 belong to partners whose own rows are flagged for the postal stream. Ms Yeo recorded that the postal manifest for job A lists row number, name, address and lodgement barcode for each of the 212 articles, with row numbers running from 12 to 5,031, and that Corbel's enveloping line keeps no record of which printed document went into which envelope. For jobs B and C she compared the e-delivery logs in the same way and, because Corbel's newer enveloping line at its second site was used for those two jobs and photographs each insert against its envelope barcode, she was also able to compare the postal articles for B and C against their manifests. No mismatch was recorded in either stream for either job.", "contacts_and_complaints": "As at 11:00 today the contact centre had logged 37 contacts about the matter: 29 by telephone, 6 by in-app message and 2 by email. Every one of the 37 is from a partner who appears in the list of 1,100. Thirty-four reported receiving someone else's statement. Three had been told by an acquaintance that their statement had gone to that acquaintance; two of those three know each other from the same airport rank. No contact has been received from any partner in the postal stream, and none from jobs B or C. Two partners have said they will complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner. One partner, a family violence survivor whose address is suppressed on the platform, has asked for a call back from a senior person; Ms Delacroix telephoned her at 10:05 today. The contact centre script issued on Tuesday afternoon tells staff to say that 'around 1,100 partners in parts of Brisbane' are involved and that those partners will be written to.", "people_and_capacity": "The partner contact centre at Bowen Hills has 14 staff on the roster this week, two of whom are on approved leave. Mr Bhattarai reports that the 37 contacts, each taking between 20 and 45 minutes including the call back, have produced a backlog of roughly two working days on ordinary enquiries such as payout queries and document uploads. Two team members have asked for a break from the incident queue after difficult calls; both have been offered the employee assistance program and one has taken it up. Mr Bhattarai's estimate, given to the scribe this morning, is that any written notice generates contact from about one in six of those who receive it within the first three days, based on the fee change notice in March. Overtime has been approved for the coming fortnight up to a ceiling of 120 hours in total. A temporary agency has quoted for four additional agents from Monday 21 July, subject to a day's induction. Identity support from the company's provider, IDGuard Australia, is contracted at a per-enrolment price with no minimum; the provider has confirmed capacity for up to 8,000 enrolments this month.", "earlier_incident_referred_to_in_discussion": "Several attendees have referred to the payout SMS matter of November 2023 (INC-PRV-2023-019). On that occasion a payout confirmation SMS containing first name, payout amount and the last three digits of a bank account was sent to the previous holder of a recycled mobile number in 86 cases. The company wrote to the 86 partners whose details had been disclosed and, where they could be identified, asked the recipients to delete the message. It did not write to anyone else. The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner was informed and closed its file without further action in February 2024. Mr Rawiri has said on two occasions this week that the 2023 approach, of writing only to those confirmed, was accepted then and should be the model now. Ms Delacroix has said that in 2023 the full set of messages sent was available from the SMS gateway log and that every message had been accounted for before the letters went out. The post-incident review of the 2023 matter recorded one criticism from partner representatives: that the letter arrived nine days after the first partner had raised it.", "contract_terms_noted_by_legal": "Mr Venkataraman has provided the following extracts from MSA-2022-114 without comment on their effect. Clause 14.2: the supplier will notify the company without undue delay of any event in which personal information is delivered to a person other than the intended recipient. Clause 14.5: the supplier will bear the reasonable and documented cost of notices, call handling and identity support arising from such an event where it results from the supplier's processing. Clause 14.6: the company will consult the supplier before issuing any notice that names the supplier. Clause 21.1: the supplier will retain production logs for each job for 90 days. Clause 21.3: on request the supplier will make available for inspection any undelivered or returned articles. Mr Hallam has indicated by telephone that Corbel accepts clause 14.5 applies and has asked that the company keep records of overtime and agency cost. Corbel's insurer has asked for the number of persons affected; Mr Hallam gave the figure of 1,100 on Wednesday afternoon.", "reissue_arrangements": "Partner Payments has confirmed that correct statements for all partners in job A can be published to the documents area of the partner app, which sits behind the partner's own login, by Friday 18 July at midday. Publishing to the app does not depend on the vendor. Partners who do not use the app, of whom there are 140 in job A, would need another channel; Partner Payments holds a mobile number for all but nine of them. A reissue by post through a second mailhouse has been costed and would take six working days from instruction. Ms Yeo has said that the list of partners for any chosen group can be produced from the merge file within an hour of the group being settled, including service address, email where held, mobile number where held and delivery stream flag.", "wellbeing_and_rostering_notes": "People & Culture has met with Mr Bhattarai's two shift leads. Both described the calls as longer and more personal than the team is used to, and said partners frequently ask a question the script does not answer, namely who has seen their details. The script has been amended to allow staff to say that the company knows which individual received each emailed document and will tell the partner concerned on request after an identity check. Shift leads asked that any further notice be sent early in the day and early in the week where possible, so that the peak in calls does not fall on a weekend roster of four. Rostered days off have not been cancelled. One request to work from home during the incident period has been approved on medical grounds.", "views_recorded_at_wednesday_stand_up": ["Mr Rawiri (Head of Partner Operations) said the company should write to the 1,100 who received a wrong statement, ask them to delete it and confirm deletion, and keep the message short. He said the 1,100 figure has been confirmed twice, by the vendor and by the company's own team, and that in his view it is settled.", "Ms Delacroix (Privacy Officer) said the people whose information was disclosed matter at least as much as the people who received it, and that her draft notification list is built from both: the 1,100 recipients and the owners of the 1,100 documents. She said she was comfortable that the figure was reliable as it had been reconciled independently.", "Mr Venkataraman (Legal Counsel) asked whether it would be simpler and safer to write to every partner in job A. Mr Bhattarai replied that the 3,730 whose hashes matched had received exactly what they should have, and asked what the contact centre would tell them when they rang.", "Ms Okonkwo (Chief Operating Officer, chair) asked whether anything outside job A needed to be considered, given that all three jobs ran on the same night with the same vendor and that job C includes partners from the same postcode band. She asked for the Data & Insights results on B and C before the group met again.", "Mr Hallam of Corbel joined for ten minutes and repeated that the stream had been fully reconciled and that the number would not change.", "Ms Delacroix noted that a first-round notice should go out no later than Friday morning and that a second round could follow if facts changed, but that in her experience second rounds are poorly received."], "remediation_elements_under_discussion": "A written notice by email and in-app message (and by SMS where no email is held); a request to recipients to delete the document and confirm; an offer of twelve months of IDGuard enrolment to those whose details were disclosed; a dedicated call-back line; for anyone who may yet receive a wrong document, a request to return it unopened or destroy it, with a reply-paid envelope to follow; reissue of correct statements through the partner app rather than through the vendor.", "other_matters_recorded": ["the ABN and bank details shown on the statement are the same on page 1 for every partner layout; page 2 carries the monthly breakdown.", "Partner Payments has suspended further jobs with Corbel pending the review. Bands 4300 and above were due to run on Monday 21 July.", "Corporate Affairs has prepared holding lines that refer to 'a delivery error by a supplier affecting some partners in Brisbane'.", "Ms Delacroix's assessment of whether the matter is an eligible data breach is in progress and is not covered by this note."]}

"Gesprächsnotiz, diktiert. Mittwoch 13. November 2024, kurz nach halb fünf Lagos-Zeit, ich sitz im Auto vor dem Büro in Ikeja, Stau auf der Obafemi Awolowo Way, also hab ich Zeit. Jonas Reuter, Vertrieb DACH, Savanna Clinical Research. Telefonat mit Frau Dr. Miriam Hartwig, Rhenovia Biotech, Basel, Clinical Operations. Ging um die Sache mit StudyDesk. Dauer gut 35 Minuten. Die Notiz hier hängt ja eh automatisch an ihrem Kontakt sobald ich auflege, also nur der Inhalt.

Worum es geht. Sie hat letzten Donnerstag im Sponsorenportal den Assistenten gefragt, wie lange NAFDAC für die Genehmigung einer klinischen Prüfung braucht. Antwort vom Assistenten, ich lese vor was sie mir weitergeleitet hat, Zitat: Die NAFDAC nennt für die Prüfung eines vollständigen Antrags einen Richtwert von rund 60 Arbeitstagen, das ist keine verbindliche Frist. Zitat Ende. Dahinter als Quelle ein Link, nafdac punkt gov punkt ng, dann Schrägstrich wp-content, uploads, clinical-trial-guidelines-2023 punkt pdf. Im selben Absatz noch zwei Quellen mit unseren Dokumentnummern in eckigen Klammern, D-2291 und D-0874, die gehören aber zu dem Satz über die Ethikkommission NHREC, nicht zu den 60 Tagen.

der link geht nicht. Fehlerseite, 404. Sie hat am Dienstag ihre Zeitschiene in der internen Projektrunde gezeigt, ihr Chef, Herr Brändli, wollte die Quelle sehen, sie klickt drauf, nichts. Wörtlich: da stand ich ziemlich blöd da. Danach hat sie einen halben Tag auf der NAFDAC-Seite gesucht und nichts gefunden. Nach draußen ist nichts gegangen, das hat sie dreimal gesagt. Nichts an die Behörde, nichts an die Prüfzentren in Lagos und Ibadan, nichts an den Vorstand. Nur die interne Runde. Nichts rausgegangen.

Was Tunde sagt. Ich hab vor dem Call mit Tunde Adebayo aus der Entwicklung gesprochen. Er hat das Protokoll gezogen, Anfrage Q-58813. Abgerufen wurden fünf Textstücke: D-2291, D-0874, zweimal SOP-RA-017, einmal D-1140, das ist die Gebührentabelle in Naira. Der Link steht in keinem der fünf, auch nicht irgendwo im Fließtext. Im Index war er nie, Tunde hat die Historie durchgesehen, auch die alten Stände vom Frühjahr. Die NAFDAC-Links die wir tatsächlich im Index haben sehen fast genauso aus, gleicher Pfad, gleiche Schreibweise, nur mit 2020 am Ende. Emeka Obi aus Regulatory sagt, eine Fassung von 2023 kennt er nicht und die hat es auch nie gegeben, gültig ist die Leitlinie von 2020, das PDF hat er, ist öffentlich, liegt bei NAFDAC ganz normal auf der Seite.

Inhaltlich. In SOP-RA-017, Abschnitt 4.2, steht, ich lese ab: Für die Bewertung vollständiger Anträge gibt NAFDAC in der Leitlinie von 2020 eine Zielgröße von etwa sechzig Arbeitstagen an, ein Anspruch auf Entscheidung innerhalb dieser Zeit besteht nicht. Das war eins der fünf Stücke. Die SOP trägt oben den Vermerk vertraulich, nur für internen Gebrauch Savanna. Der Assistent darf daraus schöpfen, so ist es eingerichtet, aber rausgeben tun wir SOPs an Sponsoren nicht, das war schon bei der Ausschreibung von Rhenovia so, da haben sie danach gefragt und wir haben nein gesagt.

Zum Prüfer. Tunde sagt der Zitat-Checker schaut nur auf die Dokumentnummern in eckigen Klammern, ob die in der abgerufenen Menge sind. Nackte Links lässt er durch, weil die Textstücke selber Links enthalten dürfen. Eine Prüfung für Links kommt frühestens im übernächsten Sprint, also Mitte Dezember, und auch nur wenn Ngozi das hochpriorisiert, sie entscheidet nächsten Dienstag.

Wie das Gespräch lief. Ich hab mich entschuldigt, nicht rumdiskutiert, hab ihr erklärt was wir bis jetzt wissen, also dass der Link nicht aus unseren Dokumenten kommt. Sie war sachlich, am Ende eigentlich ganz entspannt. Ich hab zugesagt: schriftliche Erklärung bis Freitag. Und ich hab ihr gesagt, ab nächster Woche gibt StudyDesk keine nackten Links mehr aus, dann ist das Thema erledigt. Das hat sie gefreut, sie will das so an Herrn Brändli weitergeben.

Was sie will. Wörtlich: schicken Sie mir einfach die Stelle wo das steht, dann kann ich das Herrn Brändli zeigen und gut ist. Und: ich will kein Fass aufmachen, mir reicht wenn es nicht wieder passiert. Freitag reicht ihr für die Erklärung, hat sie zweimal gesagt, Freitag reicht völlig. Nebenbei, schon halb im Auflegen: morgen früh um neun geht ihre Folie mit der Zeitschiene an den CMO, mit oder ohne Quelle, hat sie gelacht.

Fällt mir gerade ein. Im August hatte Frau Okafor-Lenz von Helvia Pharma, die mit der Studie in Kano, auch einen toten Link in einer StudyDesk-Antwort gemeldet. Das hat der Support damals als Tippfehler der Nutzerin geschlossen, ins Protokoll hat keiner geschaut.

Noch was zum Schluss. Tunde hat seit heute Mittag ein Ticket dazu, SD-4471, da steht aber nur die technische Seite drin. Was die Kundin mir heute gesagt hat, also Chef wollte die Quelle sehen, CMO morgen früh, Freitag was Schriftliches, das muss dahin wo Tunde es sieht. Ins CRM schaut er nicht. Bitte das als nächstes erledigen.

Sonstiges. Vertragsverlängerung Rhenovia steht im Februar an, Jahresvolumen rund 38 Millionen Naira. Sie fliegt am 2. Dezember nach Lagos zum Site-Besuch, Mittagessen in Victoria Island ist angedacht. Ende der Notiz."

"INTERNAL NOTE - Seller Risk Review queue | case SRR-2026-08841 | logged by: Ifeoma A. (Seller Care, Ibadan desk) | 17/09/2026 15:40

Seller: Agbedotun Farm Supplies (store id S-NG-204117), Oyo town. Owner: Alhaji Rasaq Agbedotun. On FarmKart since Feb 2024.
Why in queue: 3rd policy strike inside 60 days -> auto review.

Snapshot from seller dashboard (as at today):
- rating 4.9 (1,312 reviews)
- orders: June 214, July 298, Aug 371, Sept to date 260
- order mix last 90 days: knapsack sprayers, drip kits, tarpaulins, hand tools = about 7 in every 10 orders; agrochemicals + seed = the rest
- refunds/returns 0.8%. no open buyer disputes
- strikes before this window: none
- payout cycle weekly, last payout ₦4,870,500 on 14/09

Strikes:
1) 24/07 - late dispatch. 19 orders shipped 3-5 days after promise date. Same week the GIG Logistics Ibadan hub was shut by the drivers' strike (hub notice on file). Seller messaged every buyer himself, 2 cancelled, rest delivered.
2) 11/08 - listing for ForceUp 360SL glyphosate (1L) carried a NAFDAC reg number that lapsed 30/06. Listing taken down by catalogue team. Seller uploaded the renewed certificate 15/08, listing restored 16/08. 43 units sold while the number was lapsed. no buyer complaint on those.
3) 09/09 - SAMMAZ 52 maize seed, 10kg. Germination test certificate uploaded was for lot SC-2291, bags shipped were lot SC-2307. Catalogue team asked for the right one; seller sent the SC-2307 cert on 12/09, dated May 2026, 92% germination. 118 bags sold before the fix. No complaint so far, reviews on that listing all 5 star.

Call with seller today 14:55, 11 mins. Typing what he said as close as I could get it:

"Madam I no understand why una dey disturb me. Check my rating, 4.9. Farmers dey call me from Saki, from Iseyin, even Kwara side, because I deliver and my price correct. Planting for late maize don start, my orders dey go up every week, na now una wan block me?"

"That delivery one no be my fault, GIG people strike, everybody know."

"The glyphosate matter, na distributor never renew their paper on time. When dem renew I send am. Same product, same bottle, nothing change."

"The seed own, na my boy Sodiq dey do all the upload. Distributor go send papers for WhatsApp, Sodiq go put am. I no dey look the certificates myself, I no fit dey check every paper, na distributor work be that. If paper wrong make una tell me, I go change am like I don do."

"I get 40 cartons of atrazine and new cowpea seed wey dey land next week, I wan list am sharp sharp before rain finish."

I asked how he would feel if anything was held while we review: "No hold my money o, I dey use am restock every week. Na from payout I dey pay distributor. Farmers wey don order, na them go suffer."

He was polite all through, not shouting. wants whatever we decide sent by WhatsApp not email.

Catalogue team comment (Tunde, 16/09): "both cert issues were fixed within 4 days of our message. we picked both up ourselves on routine sampling, seller did not raise either one."

Acct manager field: (blank)
Next step owner: Seller Risk panel, Thursday sitting."

--- ORIGINAL POST --- @dr_faisal_alketbi - Mon 9 Jun 2025 8:14 PM - reposts 4,118 - quotes 612 - views 1.2M
Hello, first I am sorry to post this publicly, I am not the type who complains online and this is actually my first time buying any kind of security service so maybe some of this is my own fault for not understanding. I have a small dental clinic in Al Majaz, Sharjah (3 chairs, 6 staff). On 21 May I signed for the @HisnCyber 'Sentinel SME' package, AED 1,450 per month, because the DHA-style checklist our insurer sent says patient records need 24/7 monitoring. The onboarding was very nice, the agent was polite. BUT from 28 May untill 3 June the portal was showing 'alert forwarding: pending' and I did not know what that means, I thought it is a normal status. In those 6 days somebody logged in to our reception PC by remote desktop at 2.40 in the morning, two nights. The PC has the patient xray software on it. Nobody called me. Nobody emailed. I only found it because my receptionist said the mouse was moving by itself when she came early on 3 June. I called the hotline 3 times, I sent DM 3 times (29 May, 3 June, 4 June) and email twice with my account no. HSN-SME-20417. no answer except the auto reply. I am sorry for the long post, I just do not know where else to go. this is patients data not a late pizza.

--- REPLY 1 (same author) --- Mon 9 Jun 8:31 PM
sorry forgot to say, i am not saying the company are bad people. the sales person Mr Tariq was very kind. maybe i misunderstood the setup steps. but 6 days is 6 days

--- REPLY 2 (same author) --- Wed 11 Jun 7:05 AM - reposts 203
Update for everybody asking: to be fair to them an engineer called Hamza phoned me yesterday (Tuesday) around 4pm, he stayed on the line 1 hour, the forwarding is switched ON now and he checked the reception PC with me, changed the remote desktop settings and said he will send a written report by Sunday. so my own case is ok now alhamdulillah, I am not asking for refund or anything and sorry if my first post was too emotional. Only reason I am leaving the post up: two other clinic owners in my building messaged me after they saw it, theirs is ALSO showing 'forwarding: pending' in the portal since weeks and they also did not know what it means. one is a physio, one is a lab collection point. maybe other small customers should look at their portal also?? I dont know if it is only our building or what. sorry again for the long posts

--- TOP QUOTE POSTS (by reach) ---
@khaleej_it_guy (38k followers): 'managed' security where the managing part is optional. check your portals people
@sara_runs_a_pharmacy: just looked. mine says pending too. what is pending. @HisnCyber ??
@GulfTechWeekly: Sharjah dentist says MSSP left alerts off for six days while reception PC accessed remotely at night. We have asked Hisn Cyber for comment.
@meme_souq: 'this is patients data not a late pizza' is going on a tshirt

Home  >  Health A to Z  >  Medicines A to Z
Sertraline
Brand name: Lustral
On this page
1. About sertraline  2. Key facts  3. Who can and cannot take it  4. How and when to take it  5. Side effects  6. Taking sertraline with other medicines and painkillers  7. When to get urgent advice  8. Common questions

1. About sertraline
Sertraline is a type of antidepressant known as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). It's often used to treat depression, and also sometimes panic attacks, obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Sertraline helps many people recover from depression, and it has fewer side effects than older antidepressants. It is available on prescription only. It comes as tablets.

2. Key facts
- It usually takes 4 to 6 weeks for sertraline to work fully.
- Side effects such as feeling sick, headaches and trouble sleeping are common. They're usually mild and go away after a couple of weeks.
- You can take sertraline with or without food.
- If you and your doctor decide to take you off sertraline, your doctor will probably recommend reducing your dose gradually to help prevent extra side effects. Do not stop taking it suddenly.

3. Who can and cannot take it
Sertraline can be taken by adults for depression. Check with your doctor before starting to take sertraline if you: have had an allergic reaction to sertraline or any other medicine; have a heart problem; have ever taken any other medicines for depression; are trying to become pregnant, are already pregnant or are breastfeeding; have an eye condition called glaucoma; have epilepsy or are having electroconvulsive treatment.

4. How and when to take it
Take sertraline once a day. You can take it at any time, as long as you stick to the same time every day. If you have trouble sleeping, it's best to take it in the morning. The usual dose is 50mg a day in adults. Your dose may be increased gradually up to a maximum of 200mg a day. If you occasionally forget to take a dose, do not worry. Skip the missed dose and take your next dose the next day at the usual time. Never take 2 doses at the same time to make up for a forgotten one.

5. Side effects
Common side effects - these happen in more than 1 in 100 people and usually wear off after the first week or two: feeling sick (nausea); an unsettled stomach or diarrhoea; headaches; being unable to sleep; feeling sleepy; a dry mouth; feeling dizzy; feeling tired or weak. Keep taking the medicine but talk to your doctor or pharmacist if these side effects bother you or do not go away.
Show all sections   Hide all sections

6. Taking sertraline with other medicines and painkillers
Some medicines and sertraline can affect each other and increase the chances of you having side effects. Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you're taking: any other medicines for depression; medicines that affect your heartbeat; blood thinners such as warfarin or apixaban; migraine medicines called triptans; tramadol.
Herbal remedies: do not take St John's wort while you are being treated with sertraline.

Painkillers
Paracetamol - it's safe to take paracetamol with sertraline. Do not take paracetamol alongside other medicines that contain paracetamol, such as co-codamol or some cold and flu remedies, because of the risk of taking too much. Adults should have no more than 8 paracetamol-containing 500mg tablets in 24 hours in total.
Ibuprofen, aspirin and other anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) - taking these with sertraline can increase your chances of bleeding, particularly from the stomach. An occasional dose for a day or two is unlikely to cause problems for most people. Speak to a pharmacist or doctor before taking any anti-inflammatory painkiller if you: are 65 or over; have ever had a stomach ulcer or bleeding in your stomach or gut; take a blood thinner or a steroid. If you think you need an anti-inflammatory painkiller for more than 3 days in a row, speak to your doctor. They may want to prescribe an extra medicine to protect your stomach while you are taking both.

7. When to get urgent advice
Urgent advice: Call 111 or ask for an urgent GP appointment if you are taking sertraline and you: have black or tar-like poo; have blood in your vomit or your vomit looks like coffee grounds; have severe stomach pain that does not go away; get bruises that appear without a reason or bleeding that does not stop; have thoughts about harming yourself.
Immediate action required: Call 999 if you have chest pain or pressure, or sudden swelling of your lips, mouth, throat or tongue.

8. Common questions
Can I drink alcohol with it? You can drink alcohol while taking sertraline but it may make you feel sleepy. It might be best to stop drinking alcohol until you see how the medicine makes you feel.
Can I drive or ride a bike? Some people cannot concentrate properly while they're taking sertraline. It might be best to stop driving and cycling for the first few days of treatment until you know how this medicine makes you feel. It's an offence to drive a car if your ability to drive safely is affected.
Will it affect my contraception? Sertraline does not stop any type of contraception from working.
How long will I take it for? Once you're feeling better it's likely that you'll keep taking sertraline for several more months.
